title: Add the project to the name
hook: Three “notes” files need a clue that survives leaving their folders.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Attach a project identifier to exported filenames.

objective: Attach a project identifier to exported filenames.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Three “notes” files need a clue that survives leaving their folders. Which remains identifiable outside its folder? Correct option: Project-prefixed name. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred.

claims.text: A prefix carries the project identifier into the filename. The exercise makes identity visible; it does not estimate search time.
claims.source: Derivation from the explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and transformations in src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts; app documentation below provides command/filter context, not evidence of productivity gains or of every fixture-specific choice. Google Drive Help, Search for files in Google Drive, filtering and advanced search; retrieved 2026-10-13: https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2375114?hl=en . Exercise fixtures do not reproduce every Drive search behaviour.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: files. Exercise only; no measured productivity gain. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, project-prefix-filenames fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts.
